claims.text: Seeded growth followed by mild annealing will yield single-phase, compositionally uniform Pt–Pd–Au–Ag–Cu high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Pre-formed alloy nanoparticle seeds facilitate controlled epitaxial deposition of additional metals.
Mild post-synthesis annealing drives interdiffusion between the deposited shell and the seed.
Annealing-driven interdiffusion eliminates persistent compositional gradients and establishes a homogeneous alloy phase.
Greater compositional uniformity improves the distribution of catalytically active sites.
The improved active-site distribution produces superior catalytic performance relative to one-pot co-reduction products.
Pre-formed seeds provide defined nucleation sites.
Seeded deposition initially forms a core–shell architecture.
The initial core–shell architecture gradually evolves into a homogeneous high-entropy alloy phase.
Conventional one-pot co-reduction involves simultaneous and random nucleation.
Conventional one-pot co-reduction yields phase-separated, compositionally inhomogeneous nanoparticles.
Controlled delivery of different precursors can produce solid-solution HEA nanocrystals where one-pot synthesis produces phase separation.
Annealing at approximately 200–250 °C under a reducing atmosphere can promote interdiffusion without causing particle sintering.
The seeded-growth process will produce a narrower nanoparticle size distribution than one-pot co-reduction.
The seeded-growth process will produce a more homogeneous alloy phase than one-pot co-reduction.
The seeded-growth product will exhibit a higher turnover frequency than the one-pot product.
The seeded-growth product will exhibit greater catalytic selectivity than the one-pot product.
The seeded-growth product will exhibit a lower apparent activation energy than the one-pot product.
Insufficient annealing will prevent complete interdiffusion, whereas excessive annealing will cause particle coarsening and undermine the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies an initially compositionally segregated core–shell architecture, while the mechanism says seeded deposition ensures initial uniformity. This is inconsistent unless 'uniformity' is explicitly limited to particle morphology or deposition coverage rather than elemental composition.
